title: Token Skyline: KV spillover policy and graceful throttle for paged-attention
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As tenant and prompt diversity grow, our paged KV cache sees intermittent bursts that create high tail latency during prefill and decode phases. The current hard-evict policies and coarse prefilling cause two failure modes: (1) decode-wave stalls when large prefill cohorts trigger mass page reclamation and kernel rescheduling, and (2) wasteful thundering prefill of marginal fragments that increase memory churn and reduce kernel locality.

Goal: Implement a "Token Skyline" KV spillover and graceful throttle system that: (a) allows an ordered spillover of low-value KV fragments to host/DRAM as a backstop before irrevocable eviction, (b) computes a skyline score per fragment combining touch-frequency, future-prefill-likelihood, kernel-affinity, and decode-cost to drive eviction/spill decisions, and (c) integrates a decode/prefill pacing controller (graceful throttle) to smooth kernel handoffs and avoid decode stalls. The system should reduce 99th percentile prefill latency by at least 25% on mixed-length workloads without increasing average token cost by more than 5%.

High-level approach: Create a multi-tier residency model (GPU hot, staged-DRAM spill, cold-evict). Use a skyline scoring function to rank fragments for spill vs keep. Add a soft admission controller for prefill that throttles large prefill batches using decode-wave pacing hints to the kernel scheduler. Provide telemetry to surface spill/rehydrate events and include a fallback to immediate eviction under sustained memory pressure.
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile prefill latency reduction >= 25% on internal mixed workload benchmark
No more than 5% increase in average token cost across test suite
Telemetry dashboard with spill/rehydrate per-minute and skyline-score distribution
Fallback behavior documented and covered by unit + integration tests
Can toggle feature via runtime flag per-tenant without restart
implementation_notes: Design skyline_score = alpha*recency + beta*freq + gamma*prefill_probability + delta*kernel_affinity_score; weights initially 0.4/0.25/0.2/0.15
Add a spill ring buffer in host DRAM with async zero-copy copy path and a compact on-disk fallback for low-priority tenants
Kernel hints API: allow runtime to attach 'decode-wave-pacing' and 'preferred-kernel-set' metadata to prefill requests
Prefill admission controller watches moving-window memory pressure and issues time-sliced grants to large batches to avoid waveform overlap
Instrumentation: emit events on skyline score changes, spill decisions, rehydrates, and prefill grants; wire to console-telemetry and perf-dashboards
Start with a canary on dedicated-gpu pools for non-critical tenants, then expand to interactive workloads after metrics review
risks: Incorrect skyline weights could prefer keeping fragments that cause fragmentation and slow future kernels
Spill/rehydrate I/O could increase latency for critical low-latency tenants if not isolated
Admission controller mis-calibration could cause throughput regressions for high-throughput batch workloads
Complexity in kernel hint plumbing across runtime layers may require refactors in kernel selection code
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Spiked a simple skyline scorer in python against traces from feb workload. Preliminary results show high recall for low-value fragments but high false positives when using freq alone.
2026-03-04 - Marcus Nguyen: Implemented async spill path prototype in branch ENG-273999/spill-proto. Copy latency measured at ~120us for 64KB fragments on canary hw.
2026-03-06 - Performance review: Desktop benchmark (mixed seq 32/512/2048) shows 15% p99 improvement for prefill with naive pacing. Need to tighten skyline inputs to hit 25% target.

2026-03-08 - Design note: Agreed to add kernel_affinity feature that prefers fragments whose last serving kernel matched the current kernel set to preserve locality. Will add telemetry for kernel mismatch churn.

2026-03-10 - QA: Added unit tests for skyline scorer and spill idempotency. Started integration tests in k8s sim cluster. Edge case found where spill + immediate rehydrate causes double-copy; fixed by introducing in-flight rehydrate guard.
2026-03-12 - PM sync (K. Morales): Scoped rollout plan. Canary on dedicated pools for low-impact tenants, gate for enterprise customers after 2 weeks and SLA checks.
